messages:
maya: Quick sync — PRD draft for Optimize Toolkit (batching/caching/quant) is up. Need to agree on acceptance criteria + minimum viable scope for initial launch. Link: https://go/repo/optimize-prd

jonathan: skimmed, looks good. two asks from infra: drafting autoscaling boundary for batching and fallback when KV cache misses.

liz: can we limit initial quantization to INT8 + FP16 fallback? customers asked for deterministic output for audits.

prashant: +1. Acceptance criteria proposal:
- measurable perf: 20% token cost reduction on 90th percentile for cortex-like workloads
- latency SLOs preserved: p95 increase <= 10ms
- deterministic mode documented
- rollout path w/ canary & rollback

sarah: edge cases to call out:
- short prompt workloads (<=16 tokens) should not be batched
- streaming clients should get partial tokens asap
- degraded cache (eviction storm) — auto-fallback to cold model

maya: adding minimal config snippet for canary:
```
optimize:
  batching:
    enabled: true
    max_delay_ms: 10
    max_batch_size: 64
  quant:
    mode: int8
    fallback: fp16
  caching:
    prefix_cache: true
    ttl_ms: 300000
```

jonathan: ops note: need a metric for 'cache-induced variance' — track outputs-per-prompt diff vs baseline.

deploy-bot: canary deployment scheduled by maya for 2026-03-28 18:00 UTC :rocket:

prashant: launch checklist suggestions:
- unit + integration tests for batching knobs
- perf benchmark harness w/ reproducible seeds
- docs: deterministic behavior & known regressions
- staged rollout plan (10% -> 50% -> 100%)

liz: customer-facing docs must include rollback instructions and how to pin model variant.

maya: ok let's lock acceptance criteria with these changes. i'll update PRD and tag for review. thanks! :thumbsup:
